customConfig.name: aboutP1
customConfig.label: Homepage bio (paragraph 1)
customConfig.value: I'm Cassie, a licensed therapist who is endlessly curious about people, relationships, and what makes us who we are. My work is grounded in the belief that our experiences and relationships shape how we see ourselves and move through the world. I'm particularly interested in helping individuals and couples better understand those patterns, make room for the parts of themselves they may have learned to hide, and build deeper, more meaningful connections.

customConfig.name: aboutP2
customConfig.label: Homepage bio (paragraph 2)
customConfig.value: I believe therapy can hold both depth and lightness. It's a place for honesty, vulnerability, and sometimes a little laughter, too. My approach is thoughtful, relational, and collaborative, with room for curiosity, compassion, and the complexities of being human.

customConfig.name: aboutPageLead
customConfig.label: About page — intro line under the title
customConfig.value: I'm Cassie, a licensed therapist (but I'm guessing you already knew that if you made it to this page) practicing in Minnesota. I specialize in individual and couples therapy.

customConfig.name: aboutPageIntro
customConfig.label: About page — opening line (shown in italic serif)
customConfig.value: I've always been fascinated by people.

customConfig.name: aboutPageP1
customConfig.label: About page — story paragraph 1
customConfig.value: Have you ever been at a holiday dinner and watched a relative do something you'd never expect and wonder, Why do they do that? Chances are if you are human and have been alive for a while, you've asked that question about many people — even yourself. I ask that question all the time. Thankfully for me, there is a whole field dedicated to understanding human behavior. Even more thankfully, the work of therapy exists so we can understand not just human behavior, but all the complex facets that make us human — the stories we carry, the ways we learn to navigate relationships, and the parts of ourselves we sometimes feel we need to hide.

customConfig.name: aboutPageP2
customConfig.label: About page — story paragraph 2
customConfig.value: That curiosity is a big part of what drew me to psychotherapy. I'm especially interested in the ways our experiences and relationships shape who we become, how we connect with others, and how we understand ourselves. I love helping individuals and couples explore those layers with curiosity, compassion, and a little humor along the way.

customConfig.name: aboutPageP3
customConfig.label: About page — story paragraph 3
customConfig.value: I believe therapy, at its core, is about curiosity. It starts with asking questions, then being brave enough to find the answers we need. My goal for any client I sit with — whether individual or couple — is that you end our time together having more understanding of and compassion for yourself.

customConfig.name: aboutPageWorkPre
customConfig.label: About page — link to The Work (text before the link)
customConfig.value: To learn more about my approach to therapy and what happens in session, take a look at

customConfig.name: workIntro
customConfig.label: Homepage intro paragraph (HTML allowed)
customConfig.value: I use the word work intentionally here. Therapy is many things, and effortful is one of them. It is not easy to sit in places inside ourselves and in emotions we try hard to avoid, to look at things we usually turn away from, to talk with our partner about a topic that has somehow, in some unspoken way, become off-limits. It's hard to believe that a process often described with words like healing, holding space, journey, discovery, growth can also be associated with tears, fear, anxiety, sadness, and grief. Ah, the human experience — full of paradoxes and complexity. Thank goodness I love both of those things!

customConfig.name: workMoreText
customConfig.label: Text before the dive-deeper link
customConfig.value: I pull from a few different theories — narrative, psychodynamic, and somatic, all through an attachment framework.

customConfig.name: workDiveLabel
customConfig.label: Dive-deeper link text (links to your The Work page; leave empty to hide)
customConfig.value: Explore how each one might show up in our work together →

customConfig.name: workBeliefsLabel
customConfig.label: Beliefs — intro label
customConfig.value: A few of my beliefs in therapy:

value.text: I believe the process of getting to know ourselves, meeting all parts of ourselves and our stories with compassion, and bringing all we are to our relationships in an authentic, intimate way is one of the most rewarding things we will ever do in life.
I believe therapy is sacred work.
I believe we need humor in life and also the therapy room.

I believe that when our relationship with our partner feels secure, loving, and embracing, we can face almost anything in life. When our relationship feels like we're walking on eggshells and covered in tension, the rest of our lives feels like crap too.
I believe that people are complex and inherently good.

customConfig.name: workPageP1
customConfig.label: The Work page — paragraph 1 (HTML allowed)
customConfig.value: I use the word work intentionally here. Therapy is many things, and effortful is one of them. It is not easy to sit in places inside ourselves and in emotions we try hard to avoid, to look at things we usually turn away from, to talk with our partner about a topic that has somehow, in some unspoken way, become off-limits. It's hard to believe that a process often described with words like healing, holding space, journey, discovery, growth can also be associated with tears, fear, anxiety, sadness, and grief. Ah, the human experience — full of paradoxes and complexity. Thank goodness I love both of those things!

customConfig.name: workPageP2
customConfig.label: The Work page — paragraph 2 (HTML allowed)
customConfig.value: I pull from a few different theories in my practice. Most notably, I take a narrative, psychodynamic, and somatic approach to therapy, all through an attachment framework. If you read that and are thinking, What on earth does that mean?! Awesome. Look at you, already asking great questions! Here's a little more about what each of those approaches means and how they might show up in our work together.

value.name: Narrative
value.text: The stories we tell ourselves are powerful. We all have stories about who we are, how the world works, and what we can expect from others. Some of those stories come from our families, our experiences, and the cultures we're part of. Together, we'll get curious about the stories you've been carrying, where they came from, and whether they're still serving you.

value.name: Psychodynamic
value.text: Our early experiences matter. Some of our work will involve exploring your early experiences, family of origin, and the ways those experiences continue to shape how you relate to yourself and others. We'll also pay attention to the emotions, expectations, and relational patterns that emerge in the therapy room itself. Sometimes, what happens between us can offer valuable insight into what happens in other relationships.

value.name: Somatic
value.text: Our body holds important knowledge and we need to be able to connect to it. What are you feeling in your body? Can you sense it? What happens in your body when you're overwhelmed, anxious, or triggered? Our bodies hold experiences and information that we don't always have words for. Through a somatic lens, we'll make room for that knowledge and explore how your nervous system responds to the world around you.

translations.emptyState: Click the button to add your first approach card

customConfig.name: attachmentText
customConfig.label: Featured card — paragraph
customConfig.value: Our relationships matter. This is the framework at the heart of my work. At its core is a simple but important idea: our relationships matter. The ways we've experienced connection, safety, and belonging shape how we understand ourselves and how we show up with others. And this doesn't stop with our early relationships — our partnerships, friendships, and even work relationships continue to influence us.

customConfig.name: attachmentQuestionsLabel
customConfig.label: Featured card — questions label
customConfig.value: Questions we might sit with together:

customConfig.name: attachmentQuestions
customConfig.label: Featured card — questions (list items; HTML <li> allowed)
customConfig.value:
• Who have you learned you need to be in order to feel loved or accepted?
  • What do you believe others expect of you?
  • Do you find yourself performing, placating, withdrawing, or pushing others away when relationships feel difficult?
  • What happens when you need something from someone else?

customConfig.name: attachmentNote

customConfig.value: These are just some of the questions we might explore together.

customConfig.name: faqIntro
customConfig.label: Intro text (beside the questions)
customConfig.value: Starting therapy brings up a lot of questions — that's more than okay. Here are the ones I hear most often.

customConfig.name: sessionCostFee
customConfig.label: Fee line (shown large & bold)
customConfig.value: My standard fee is $175 for a 50-minute session.

customConfig.name: sessionCostP1
customConfig.label: Session cost paragraph 1
customConfig.value: At this time, I have chosen to operate as a private-pay practice and do not bill insurance directly. This wasn't a decision I made lightly. I recognize that insurance coverage can make therapy more accessible and affordable for many people. At the same time, choosing not to work directly with insurance allows for greater flexibility and autonomy in how I practice and how we approach our work together.

customConfig.name: sessionCostP2
customConfig.label: Session cost paragraph 2
customConfig.value: I believe therapy should be accessible to everyone, not just those who can comfortably afford it. With that in mind, I reserve a limited number of spaces in my practice for clients seeking a reduced fee through a sliding scale.

customConfig.name: sessionCostP3
customConfig.label: Session cost paragraph 3
customConfig.value: If you're interested in a sliding-scale space, or if the cost of therapy feels like a barrier, please reach out. Even if I don't have a reduced-fee opening available, I'm happy to talk through other options or help you explore ways to access support.

value.question: How does online therapy work?
value.answer: All sessions are held online via a secure, HIPAA-compliant video platform — from wherever you feel most comfortable, anywhere in Minnesota.

value.question: How do I know if we're a good fit?
value.answer: That's exactly what the free 15–20 minute consultation is for. It's a low-pressure conversation to see if my style and approach feel right for you. If not, I'm glad to offer referrals.

value.question: Is everything confidential?
value.answer: Yes. Your privacy is protected by law and by my own ethical commitment. The only exceptions are standard legal duties around imminent harm, which we'll discuss in our first session.
